findings.title: Unescaped external JSON fields written into HTML response
findings.explanation: The REST endpoint streams JSON fetched from a remote, attacker-influenceable source (Flickr's public "recent photos" feed, to which any Flickr user can contribute by uploading a photo) and writes the id, server, secret, and farm field values directly into an HTML document via PrintWriter.println without any HTML-encoding or sanitization (line 74: ""). Because the resource is annotated @Produces("text/html") and returned directly to any client calling GET /parser, any of these JSON string values that contain characters such as \" or < can break out of the attribute/tag context and inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that executes in the browser of whoever requests this endpoint, resulting in a cross-site scripting vulnerability.
